# Paṭhamajananakuhana Sutta (Iti 35 (It 2.8 PTS It 28))

**ID:** Iti 35 (It 2.8 PTS It 28)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Paṭhamajananakuhana Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Deceit and Flattery (1st)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭhamajananakuhana Sutta* ("Deceit and Flattery (1st)", Iti 35) is a discourse found in the second section of the *Itivuttaka* (It 2.8, PTS It 28) [SuttaCentral]. The text teaches that the holy life (*brahmacariya*) is not undertaken for the sake of deceiving or flattering people, but rather for the purpose of restraint and abandoning [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies a full Chinese parallel at T 765.76 (律儀), along with passage-level parallels in the *Brahmacariya Sutta* (AN 4.25), the directly following *Dutiyajananakuhana Sutta* (Iti 36), and T 765.75 (為通達) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms substantial Pali-internal textual overlap corresponding to these relationships, identifying extensive shared phrasing with the *Dutiyajananakuhana Sutta* (Iti 36, segments §0.1–5.1) and AN 4 (AN 4.25, segments §2.1–4.6), as well as smaller shared segments with the *Somanassa Sutta* (Iti 37), the *Bahukāra Sutta* (Iti 107), and the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā* [DharmaNexus]. The discourse has been translated into fifteen languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
